newsitem.title: FRANCE: Mercedes aims for 200,000 A car sales - paper.
newsitem.headline: Mercedes aims for 200,000 A car sales - paper.

text.p: Mercedes-Benz AG chairman Helmut Werner said in an interview with a French newspaper published on Monday that the group was targetting sales of 200,000 Class A cars in the medium term.
Mercedes is unveiling an A class minicar at the Paris car show which opens on Thursday.
"For the future A class, on a potential global market of eight million vehicles, we're aiming for 200,000 units in the medium term," Werner told the French newspaper Figaro.
"We also hope to sell 200,000 units of the little Smart, conceived with the Swiss Swatch group. Altogether, Mercedes should sell 1.1 million cars around the year 2000," he said.
Although Mercedes is broadening its range, Werner stressed that the group was not becoming a mass producer.

"One thing is certain, we will never be a generalist. It would be the end of Mercedes. We will be in top of the line in all the market segments. We're not going to cheapen the brand by putting out a small car," he said.

"Customers of our high-end models, like the E class, also want to buy small or different cars. We're therefore transposing the Mercedes philosophy on innovative segments with the launches from now to 1998 of nine new models," he said. The launches include a multi-purpose vehicle and a four-by-four.
The launches will require investments of 25 billion German marks that will be covered by the carmaker's cashflow, he said.

Werner said the group also aimed to recapture market share in industrial vehicles through the introduction in October of the Actros truck line. Mercedes aims to increase its share to over 30 percent in Europe from 25 percent currently.

"Actros should contribute around 500 million German marks toward the improvement of the division's results and we confirm our objective to pull the truck operation in Europe out of the red by 1998," he said. He said Mercedes aims for a 12 percent return on investment in both its cars and industrial vehicles.
